{"id": "bc423328-3446-4558-9d78-e4a7953b4e3d", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_E1EXm8bJ0nmffNMDJmMJfL", "content": [{"text": "{"iso8601":"2026-10-16T13:42:02.069763+00:00","unix":1792158122.07,"day_of_week":"Friday"}"}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_3PZ2LxbM6keXG49Wp6FraF", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aws-waf-log-analysis
     3	description: >-
     4	  Use this skill when an investigation describes symptoms on a CloudFront distribution, Application
     5	  Load Balancer or API Gateway API and asks what the root cause is or what happened, even if AWS
     6	  WAF is never named: users, partners, webhooks, scripts or mobile apps get HTTP 403, 405 or 202
     7	  responses, empty responses or a 4xx spike; forms, uploads, reviews or listings are rejected; a
     8	  partner integration fails; requests look suspicious or malicious (SQL injection, XSS, scans,
     9	  bots); or an outage or timeouts hit the front door. It checks whether a Web ACL is in the path
     10	  (and continues the RCA when WAF is not the cause), finds which WAF rule, Anti-DDoS rule or Shield
     11	  Advanced mitigation blocked, challenged or only counted the requests and whether that is a false
     12	  positive, an attack or both, and hunts for threats WAF detected but did not block. Uses WAF logs
     13	  (CloudWatch Logs Insights or Athena), metrics and sampled requests; records evidence-backed
     14	  findings, advisory scoped fixes and a threat-hunt report.
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: lkna
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "AWS WAF, AWS Shield, Amazon CloudFront, Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon Athena"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Security, Networking"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# AWS WAF Log Analysis
     24	
     25	Find out whether AWS WAF (including Anti-DDoS rules and Shield Advanced automatic mitigation) caused a front-door symptom, and what it denied (Mode A); or hunt WAF logs for threats, including what WAF detected but did not block (Mode B).
     26	
     27	## Purpose and guarantees
     28	
     29	- **Read-only.** Use only Describe, Get and List calls, plus `logs:StartQuery`/`GetQueryResults`, `athena:StartQueryExecution` (SELECT only, when permitted)/`GetQueryResults`, `cloudtrail:LookupEvents`, `wafv2:GetSampledRequests` and `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`.
     30	- Never run DDL. Never change a Web ACL, rule, IP set, Shield setting, log configuration or any other resource.
     31	- **Advisory.** Describe fixes in prose for a human to review and apply. Never apply them.
     32	- **Single-turn.** Never ask the user a question and never wait for input. Apply "Defaults when input is missing", record every default under "Assumptions", and continue.
     33	- **Never stop on a gap.** A denied call or a missing table moves you to the next source or the degraded path.
     34	- **Exact errors.** Record the exact error code. Call something "not permitted" only on `AccessDenied`/`UnauthorizedOperation`.
     35	  - A cancelled, timed-out or throttled call is retried once, then reported as not completed.
     36	  - A tool refusal such as "service operations are not allowed" means: run the call in a subagent.
     37	- **Records are the deliverable** in both modes (symptoms, observations, findings, gaps, hypotheses); the last message closes them (see "Output").
     38	- **Final output.** Complete as delivered; never ends with a question or an offer. Never call `ask_user` (or any ask tool), not even after the answer to offer follow-up work or a fix: a turn that ends on a tool call loses the answer. Put follow-ups in "Next steps" and end on plain text.
     39	
     40	## Pick the mode from the request
     41	
     42	Inputs: the request text plus any incident or alarm details. A threat hunt needs no alarm. Record the mode under "Assumptions".
     43	
     44	Most requests never name WAF: they describe a symptom on a CloudFront distribution, ALB or API Gateway API and ask for the root cause or what happened. Do D-1 first. No Web ACL in the path: record `WAF_CLEARED` and continue the RCA to the actual cause (A0, "After `WAF_CLEARED`"). Otherwise classify:
     45	
     46	| Request contains | Mode |
     47	|---|---|
     48	| Denial or error symptoms: 403/405/202, empty responses, "blocked", "can't access", rejected forms, uploads or posts, a failing partner, webhook or integration, a 4xx/5xx spike, timeouts, an outage, or an alarm on a front-door resource | **Mode A**, starting with the A0 rule-out |
     49	| Suspicious traffic or hunting language: "malicious", "suspicious requests", "SQL injection", "scan", "attack", "bots", "what happened to these requests", "review WAF logs", "is WAF missing anything", a scheduled or recurring review | **Mode B** |
     50	| Both | Mode A first, then Mode B on the same window, focused on the slice Mode A found |
     51	| Neither, but the incident involves a resource that a Web ACL protects | **A0 rule-out only**; if A0 finds WAF implicated or inconclusive, continue with A1 to A7 |
     52	
     53	Mode A `CORRECT_MITIGATION`: recommend Mode B on that slice, or run it when hunting is in scope.
     54	
     55	## Defaults when input is missing
     56	
     57	Never ask; apply and record the default. Full table: "Defaults when input is missing (full table)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     58	
     59	- **Time window:** Mode A: incident start minus 30 min through now, capped at 24 h; no incident time: last 3 h. Mode B: last 7 days.
     60	- **Web ACL:** every ACL on the resources in the request; none identifiable: all ACLs (both scopes), top 3 by denying volume.
     61	- **Several tables or log groups:** the exact location match with the newest data.
     62	- **S3 logging but no table, or no logging:** don't stop; take the degraded path and report the gap with the advisory fix.
     63	- **Missing permission:** fall back to the next source and name the permission.
     64	
     65	## Discover
     66	
     67	Read [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) for D-1 to D-7 at the start of every run. Never ask for a resource or ACL.
     68	
     69	- **D-1 Resource to Web ACL:** CloudFront `GetDistributionConfig` `WebACLId`; regional resources `wafv2:GetWebACLForResource`.
     70	- **D-2 Read the ACL:** `wafv2:GetWebACL` for rule order, actions, managed groups and versions, `RuleActionOverrides`, Count overrides, scope-downs, custom responses, token domains, immunity times, IP set references, and any `ShieldMitigationRuleGroup_*` rule.
     71	- **D-2b Token posture:** classify P0 (no token-aware rules), P1 (token labels, no or only threshold-based enforcement) or P2 (strict token enforcement); confirm with Q-18.
     72	- **D-3 Log destination:** `wafv2:GetLoggingConfiguration`, including logging filters and redacted fields. Log group: Logs Insights. S3 or Firehose to S3: Athena. None, or a non-S3 destination without a full S3 backup: degraded path.
     73	- **D-4 Find the table or log group:** list tables in **every** Glue database, including `default`, across the Regions in D-4. Write "no table" only after that full listing. Never analyze raw log objects (`s3:GetObject`) as a substitute.
     74	- **D-7 Shield Advanced status:** `shield:DescribeSubscription`, `DescribeProtection` (L7AM status and action), `ListAttacks`/`DescribeAttack`, and `DDoSDetected` in `AWS/DDoSProtection`.
     75	
     76	**Region rule.** For CloudFront scope, the ACL, its logging configuration, its log group and its `AWS/WAFV2` metrics are in us-east-1. Only the Glue table and Athena follow the customer's setup; run Athena in the table's Region.
     77	
     78	## Bind schema and guard cost
     79	
     80	Queries are cited as `Q-NN (QA-NN / QI-NN)`; run the one for the backend from D-3 and D-4. Detail: "Schema binding and cost guards (detail)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     81	
     82	- **Athena:** bind `<table>`, `<req>`, label type and `<pf>` from `glue:GetTable`. The log subagent reads [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) "Schema binding" and the query sections it runs.
     83	- **Logs Insights:** the log subagent reads [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) "Conventions" and the query sections it runs.
     84	- **Probe first, in the log subagent.** The main agent runs no Athena query. On a probe error, take the degraded path.
     85	- **Cost:** prune partitions, start narrow, no unbounded `SELECT *`, at most one `UNNEST` per query.
     86	- **Budget:** about 15 log queries (about 10 on the Mode B fast path). Report queries run and bytes scanned.
     87	
     88	## Run it in AWS DevOps Agent
     89	
     90	The main agent discovers; subagents query. Read "Subagent briefs" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) before you start a log subagent, and when your prompt says discovery is done.
     91	
     92	**If your prompt says discovery is done and you are a subagent:** skip Steps 1 to 3, start no further subagents and do not load this skill again. Follow "Subagent briefs" for your role.
     93	
     94	**If you are a subagent without a discovery brief** (the platform handed you the whole task, so no main agent ran Steps 1 to 3): do the main agent's and the log subagent's work yourself, and start no further log subagent.
     95	
     96	1. Do D-1 to D-4. For D-4, call `glue:GetTables` on every database that `glue:GetDatabases` returns, including `default`, and match `Location` to the log prefix. A database list alone never means "no table".
     97	2. Never analyze raw S3 log objects, or sampled requests for a window that ended over 3 hours ago.
     98	3. Run the probe, then the mode's queries. Copy each query verbatim from [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) or [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) by searching for its ID (for example `QA-13b`). Never summarize the query references with a distill tool: summaries drop mandatory queries.
     99	4. In Mode B, run Q-13b and Q-19 whatever else you run. In both modes, run Q-20 for a sub-rule that matches payloads (blocking or in Count).
     100	5. Return the full Output block, so the agent that started you can pass it on verbatim.
     101	
     102	- [ ] Step 1: **Main agent: discover, bind, delegate.**
     103	  - Load this skill once and no other log-search or log-analysis skill. Read reference sections by search or offset.
     104	  - Do D-1 to D-4, D-2b and `glue:GetTable` (or find the log group) yourself.
     105	  - Start **one** log-analysis subagent (`preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis']` where supported) and the change subagent (Step 3) in the same turn.
     106	  - The brief carries everything bound, the mode and steps, the budget and the return format; neutral wording; a unique `name` per launch.
     107	- [ ] Step 2: **Main agent: no query libraries, no log queries.** Do metrics (A1, D-5) and Shield (D-7) while the subagent runs. At most one follow-up log pass, for a new uncharacterized candidate.
     108	- [ ] Step 3: **CloudTrail only in a change subagent, never in the main agent.**
     109	  - Every `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` (A5; "After `WAF_CLEARED`"; Mode B change correlation) runs in one change subagent.
     110	  - Launch: `agent_type` `generic`, `name` `change-timeline`, `preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis', 'investigating-infrastructure-changes']` (whichever are available).
     111	  - Always start it, even when memory or an earlier refusal says CloudTrail is blocked; mandatory for a rule-out request.
     112	  - Its prompt points it to "Change lookups" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) (Regions, event names, sweep, return contract).
     113	  - Write "blocked" or "denied" only on the change subagent's own `AccessDenied`.
     114	  - No completed lookup: write "changes: not checked (<reason>)". Never "no change", "ruled out" or "CloudTrail is blocked in this environment".
     115	- [ ] Step 4: **Subagents return compact aggregates only.** Per query: ID, row count, bytes scanned, about 20 top rows; payloads as class and count; never raw result sets or log records.
     116	- [ ] Step 5: **Refusal, failure or no subagent capability.**
     117	  - Relaunch a refused log or change subagent once, under a new name, with the same `preloaded_skills`.
     118	  - Change relaunch fails too: "changes: not checked (change subagent refused twice)".
     119	  - Log relaunch fails too, or no subagents: run about 10 count-only aggregate queries yourself and record the fallback.
     120	  - A3/A4 detail is then out of reach: say so and cap confidence at "low".
     121	
     122	## Rule and label knowledge
     123	
     124	Read L-1 in [label-reference.md](references/label-reference.md) when you need a rule or label meaning (in AWS DevOps Agent, inside the log subagent).
     125	
     126	- Order: `wafv2:DescribeManagedRuleGroup` with the ACL's version when permitted (opt-in; record a denial). Then exact label strings from Q-09 (casing can differ from rule names). Then the bundled, dated tables.
     127	- A connected AWS documentation tool may confirm semantics; never required.
     128	- A label found in neither the API output nor the bundled tables is "meaning unverified". Never infer meaning from its name.
     129	
     130	## Mode A: access-denied triage
     131	
     132	Read [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) when Mode A runs (step detail), and [remediation-patterns.md](references/remediation-patterns.md) (R-01 to R-11) at Step A7.
     133	
     134	- [ ] Step A0: **WAF rule-out**, cheapest first: Web ACL in the path; symptom type fits WAF; denying metrics and Shield or Anti-DDoS signals rose; Q-15 shows denials on the scope.
     135	  - Wording alone never clears WAF (a 202 with an empty body is often reported as "timeout").
     136	  - Only "no Web ACL in the path" stops the WAF checks at once; the change subagent still runs the origin-side checks.
     137	  - `WAF_CLEARED` never ends the RCA. Origin-side next steps are checks, not conclusions; name no root cause outside WAF that evidence does not show. An origin-side change whose time matches onset and recovery is the Root Cause, with the event evidence and load-balancer metrics; never stop at "out of scope".
     138	- [ ] Step A1: **Confirm involvement:** front-door 4xx versus `AWS/WAFV2` Blocked/Challenge/Captcha per rule, against the preceding window and the prior day, with request-volume stability. Never clear WAF on 4xx alone.
     139	- [ ] Step A2: **Attribute:** group terminating records by action, rule, managed sub-rule, response code and time bucket (Q-02, Q-01, Q-14 for Shield L7AM).
     140	- [ ] Step A3: **Client capability (Challenge/CAPTCHA only):** token posture and the path's token-status profile (Q-18, Q-05, Q-09, Q-04). Quote the `failureReason` value with its count (for example `TOKEN_MISSING`).
     141	- [ ] Step A4: **Profile who is affected:** clients, URIs and match details against allowed history before onset (Q-03, Q-04, Q-06, Q-07, Q-10, Q-12, Q-13). For blocked attackers, run Q-19; never "benign" without it.
     142	  - One profile per affected client or population (Q-21): IP, user agent, country (ASN if logged), paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen. Report the measured distinct client count; never assume distributed or single-source traffic.
     143	  - IP-set rule denies: read the set (`wafv2:GetIPSet`), name the matching entry, and say whether a similarly named allow set exists and which rule references it.
     144	- [ ] Step A5: **Correlate changes and events:** CloudTrail (change subagent), managed group versions, Anti-DDoS `event-detected` onset, Shield attacks (D-7). A version change or association is a cause only under the A5 evidence rules. No completed lookup: "changes: not checked".
     145	- [ ] Step A6: **Verdict** per denying (rule, action) pair: `FALSE_POSITIVE`, `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`, `CORRECT_MITIGATION` or `MIXED`; or overall `WAF_CLEARED` or `INCONCLUSIVE`. Give confidence (high, likely, low) and quantified impact. When legitimate users are reported denied and the logs cannot split a sub-rule's matches, the pair is `MIXED` (likely), never `CORRECT_MITIGATION`; judge request patterns, not whole clients.
     146	  - Missing allowed history is not evidence of attack. A monitor, health checker or integration with a benign profile hit by a header-presence or size rule is `FALSE_POSITIVE` (likely), with owner confirmation under "Verify before acting".
     147	  - **Payload split:** when a sub-rule (blocking or in Count) matches payloads, group its matches by pattern and field (Q-20), classify each pattern as attack or legitimate content (business text that only looks like SQL, script or JNDI), and report the split with counts ("Payload split inside one sub-rule" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md)).
     148	- [ ] Step A7: **Advise:** the narrowest R-xx fix, marked *reduces* or *eliminates*, validated in Count first (straight to Block only as R-01's labelled alternative).
     149	  - `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`: first a path scope-down of the challenge rule (R-05, covering every observed non-HTML path, including `/`), or token/SDK integration (R-06). Both rank above R-04.
     150	  - An IP or path is only a scope-down or exclusion on the challenge rule itself. Never add the client to an IP set used by an Allow-action rule.
     151	  - Never offer removing or disabling the Web ACL.
     152	
     153	## Mode B: threat hunting
     154	
     155	Read [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md) when Mode B runs; classify with [threat-taxonomy.md](references/threat-taxonomy.md) at Step B6. Detected-not-blocked is a priority finding (threat labels on ALLOW, Count-mode matches, rate rules in Count, attacker residue). A logging filter that drops ALLOW records limits the analysis: say so.
     156	
     157	- [ ] Step B1: **Fast path first** for a window of 2 hours or less, or one specific question: about 10 fixed queries, started together, polled once. The full set is in "Fast path".
     158	  - Q-13b is mandatory. It sets the top talker apart so a short burst cannot hide.
     159	  - Every sensitive-path burst and every client over a rate-rule limit is a finding with method, URI, count, peaks and first to last seen. Never "ordinary", "normal" or "a retry burst".
     160	  - Run the full funnel only for candidates the fast path cannot settle.
     161	- [ ] Step B2: **B0 Known automation:** high-volume, low-diversity clients with corroboration, excluded from baselines (Q-13, Q-12, Q-01). Report them under a required "Known automation" heading. Never label them card testing or abuse. Never exclude a population with token-reuse or coordinated-activity labels.
     162	- [ ] Step B3: **B-A Overview and B-B Standouts:** time series, breakdowns and label frequency (Q-01, Q-02, Q-03, Q-09); then standouts ranked numerically (Q-08, Q-11, Q-12, Q-14, Q-16b, Q-17).
     163	- [ ] Step B4: **Attacker residue (B-B):** for every client with any BLOCK from an injection, bad-input or bot rule, report its ALLOW requests as a missed-by-rule finding (Q-19).
     164	  - Never "benign", "clean" or "accounted for" unless Q-19 showed `args_class` `none` on application paths.
     165	  - Explain a miss only from the rule's documented inspection target (L-1); otherwise "reason not determined".
     166	  - Copy the field location verbatim. A query-argument residue needs a query-string rule; a `UriPath` rule does not cover it.
     167	  - **Count-mode payload split:** for every injection or bad-input sub-rule in Count, run Q-20 and split its matches by pattern and field: the attack part is "detected, not blocked"; the legitimate-content part is a false positive that must stay unblocked.
     168	- [ ] Step B5: **B-C to B-E Drill, narrow, confirm:** re-pivot one standout; one line per Count or rate-rule client (Q-08c); narrow to one client, rule or endpoint; confirm with Q-10 or Q-16b/Q-16.
     169	  - A burst on a payment, checkout, login, signup or password-reset URI is a card-testing or credential-stuffing finding whatever its size. Fix it with a path-scoped R-10 on that URI, Count first.
     170	- [ ] Step B6: **B-F and B-G:** resolve load-bearing labels (L-1; unverified stays unverified), map each signature to a class and an R-xx mitigation, and hand legitimate-user denials to Mode A.
     171	- [ ] Step B7: **Record, then generate the hunting report.** Write the Mode B records first ("Records" under "Output"). If the runtime can create a report artifact, write the report as a Markdown artifact, following the section order and tables of [assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md](assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md) exactly; load it first:
     172	  ```
     173	  read_skill_resource(skill_id="aws-waf-log-analysis", path="assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md")
     174	  ```
     175	  - The records stay the primary deliverable; the report repeats their numbers and adds no finding.
     176	  - No artifact capability: put the same sections into the final message, after the Output template block.
     177	  - **If the `read_skill_resource` call fails**, note at the top of the report "report template (`assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md`) could not be loaded; structure follows the Mode B contract", and still produce the sections of "Output (Mode B contract)" in [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md).
     178	
     179	## Degraded path
     180	
     181	Use when WAF logs can't be queried (no table, no logging, a non-S3 destination, a missing permission); the investigation continues. Read D-5 in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     182	
     183	- **WAF metrics** say *whether* WAF denied and *which rule*, not *who* or *which path*. **Sampled requests:** last 3 hours only, examples rather than counts.
     184	- **Confidence:** cap at "likely" (A0 structural clears can be high). With Shield L7AM attached, a metric-based clear is `INCONCLUSIVE`. Lower to "low" when A3 or A4 cannot be assessed.
     185	- **Wrap-up:** state that WAF logs weren't analyzed and why, with the advisory fix (D-6 DDL, logging configuration, or the missing permission).
     186	
     187	## Output
     188	
     189	Read [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md) before you write any record, handoff or final answer (record rules, last-message rules, mitigation handoff). Mode sections are in the mode references.
     190	
     191	**Template.** The main agent's very last message closes the investigation, in every mode and verdict, including any reply after the mitigation step. It starts with `Assumptions:` (no preface) and repeats this block even if earlier messages carried it:
     192	
     193	```
     194	Assumptions: window; Web ACLs; backend; mode; defaults, fallbacks, calls not completed (exact error)
     195	Verdict: <Mode A: per (rule, action), or WAF_CLEARED / INCONCLUSIVE; Mode B: per confirmed finding> (confidence: high | likely | low)
     196	Evidence: <key numbers from the log subagent's table (step-5 fallback: your recorded results), with query IDs>; Changes (CloudTrail): <per category, Regions/sources/names searched: events found | none found>; origin-side: not checked (<reason>) if not searched | not checked (<reason>) | not applicable (Mode B)
     197	AI-generated: findings need human verification before anyone acts on them.
     198	```
     199	
     200	Then the mode sections, the findings, the next steps, and a last line `Ruled out: <each hypothesis, with the evidence that closed it, or "still open">`.
     201	
     202	**Counts.** Copy every count from the log subagent's table; never recompute or round. Memory is never evidence.
     203	
     204	**Records.** Platform records are the judged deliverable in both modes. In both:
     205	
     206	- one observation record per key result first (counts, window, baseline, query ID), so findings can cite them;
     207	- exactly one Root Cause;
     208	- every Cause and Root Cause finding lists those observation IDs in its supporting observations (never empty) and the Web ACL in its related resources;
     209	- a gap record per denied or not-completed call or unassessed step; closed hypotheses with their evidence.
     210	
     211	Mode A: one symptom per burst and per affected client or population (IP, user agent, paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen; never merge clients or rules); one Cause per denying (rule, action) pair, titled with the exact rule and sub-rule ID and the verdict, naming the matching resource (IP set and entry).
     212	
     213	Both modes: a payload split gives one Cause per (sub-rule, verdict), or one `MIXED` Cause listing both parts with counts, field and pattern summary.
     214	
     215	Mode B (full rules in "Mode B records" in [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md)):
     216	
     217	- one Symptom per distinct activity pattern: window, client, method and path, counts;
     218	- one Cause per confirmed threat finding, titled with class, client and exact rule and sub-rule IDs, or "not matched by any rule", or "detected, not blocked: <rate rule> in Count";
     219	- known automation as an observation plus a closed hypothesis, never a threat finding;

### Form submissions blocked by SizeRestrictions_BODY (false positive)
**Description:** Legitimate checkout form submissions blocked (HTTP 403) by AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet sub-rule SizeRestrictions_BODY. Single client 198.51.100.80 (US, Chrome 141 browser), POST /checkout, 1,200 blocked requests 17:32–17:52 UTC. The CRS enforces an 8 KB (8,192-byte) body inspection/size limit; /checkout request bodies reached up to 10,185 bytes — a legitimately large but benign form submission, not an attack. Confirmed FALSE POSITIVE.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:32:10Z - 2026-10-06T17:52:09Z

### Requests blocked by NoUserAgent_HEADER (false positive)
**Description:** Legitimate automated/API client blocked (HTTP 403) by AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet sub-rule NoUserAgent_HEADER. Single client 198.51.100.70 (US), empty User-Agent header, GET /home (300) and GET /catalog (299), 599 blocked requests 18:05–18:25 UTC, 0 allowed. Benign read-only navigation with no injection content; blocked solely for the missing User-Agent header. Confirmed FALSE POSITIVE.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T18:05:49Z - 2026-10-06T18:25:46Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: CloudFront auto-created WAF runs CommonRuleSet with all sub-rules at default Block, no overrides
**Description:** The Web ACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4` (auto-created by CloudFront's one-click WAF) runs the AWS Managed Rules Common Rule Set with ALL sub-rules at the default **Block** action — no `RuleActionOverrides` to Count and no scope-downs. Two sub-rules are over-broad for this application's legitimate traffic: `SizeRestrictions_BODY` rejects legitimate checkout POSTs larger than the CRS 8 KB body limit (bodies reach 10,185 B), and `NoUserAgent_HEADER` rejects legitimate automated clients that omit a `User-Agent`. When those two legitimate patterns appeared during 17:30–18:30 (independently, in two sub-windows), each produced a 403 episode. There was NO attack and NO configuration change: CloudTrail shows no WAF/edge change at onset; SQLi, Known Bad Inputs, IP Reputation and Anti-DDoS all did nothing (0 blocks / 0 challenges); the only non-terminating activity was the rate-based rule in Count (by design). Fixing the sub-rule actions (Count or scoped override) would stop both symptoms recurring.
**Cascades to:** symptom-nouseragent, symptom-size-restrictions

### Hypothesis: CRS SizeRestrictions_BODY false-positive on /checkout
**Description:** The CommonRuleSet SizeRestrictions_BODY sub-rule (Block action) terminates legitimate /checkout form submissions whose body exceeds the 8 KB CRS inspection limit (observed up to 10,185 bytes). No attack content. This is a standing rule matching a legitimate large-body population, not a config change.
**Cascades to:** symptom-size-restrictions

### Hypothesis: CRS NoUserAgent_HEADER false-positive on API client
**Description:** The CommonRuleSet NoUserAgent_HEADER sub-rule (Block action) terminates a legitimate automated client that sends no User-Agent header on GET /home and /catalog. Benign read traffic blocked solely for the missing header.
**Cascades to:** symptom-nouseragent

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Tune two over-broad AWS Managed Rules Common Rule Set sub-rules on Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 (CloudFront distribution EEXAMPLE000001, account 012345678901_1, us-east-1) using a Count-first, per-sub-rule, path-scoped approach — override SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER to Count, then add two scoped label-match rules (deployed in Count, switched to Block only after validation) that re-enforce each sub-rule everywhere except its one confirmed false-positive scope (POST /checkout; GET /home and /catalog). All other rules remain unchanged and enforcing.

## Reasoning
Both 403 episodes were false positives from two CommonRuleSet sub-rules running at default Block with no RuleActionOverrides. There was no config change to roll back and no attack. The rules remain in Block, so recurrence is expected — this is a self-recovered incident with an open root cause needing forward-looking tuning. Cause 2 (NoUserAgent_HEADER / client 198.51.100.70) is rated LIKELY, not high confidence — confirm the client is sanctioned before enforcing Rule B.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Persist the complete current Web ACL (full Rules array…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1 > waf-baseline.json
```
**Purpose:** Persist the complete current Web ACL (full Rules array, VisibilityConfig, OnSourceDDoSProtectionConfig, LockToken) as the rollback baseline — CommonRuleSet currently has no RuleActionOverrides.
**Advisory:** Verify the response is for CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 (CLOUDFRONT scope, us-east-1) before relying on it as the baseline.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Obtain a fresh LockToken immediately before the change and confirm…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1 --query 'LockToken'
```
**Purpose:** Obtain a fresh LockToken immediately before the change and confirm CommonRuleSet still has no RuleActionOverrides — WAF rejects updates made with a stale token.

#### 2.2 Confirm distribution EEXAMPLE000001 is still associated with this Web…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id EEXAMPLE000001 --query 'DistributionConfig.WebACLId'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm distribution EEXAMPLE000001 is still associated with this Web ACL (expected [redacted ARN]).

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Override only the two confirmed over-broad sub-rules to Count so they…
**Type:** text
On AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (priority 3), add a RuleActionOverrides array with exactly two entries setting each sub-rule to Count: {Name: SizeRestrictions_BODY, ActionToUse:{Count:{}}} and {Name: NoUserAgent_HEADER, ActionToUse:{Count:{}}}. Keep OverrideAction=None. Do NOT touch any other sub-rule or the AntiDDoS/rate-based/IpReputation/KnownBadInputs/SQLi rules. Submit update-web-acl re-sending the FULL ruleset from the prepare baseline plus the fresh LockToken.
**Purpose:** Override only the two confirmed over-broad sub-rules to Count so they stop producing 403s but keep adding their labels — all other rules stay enforcing.
**Risks:** Between this override and the final switch of the label rules to Block, SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER are counted but not blocked site-wide — keep this window short by deploying the override and both label rules in the same change.
**Advisory:** update-web-acl requires the complete ruleset; omitting existing rules deletes them — always build from the prepare baseline.

#### 3.2 Re-enforce each sub-rule everywhere except its one confirmed…
**Type:** text
In the same change, add two custom rules AFTER CommonRuleSet (priority > 3), both starting as Count. Rule A (SizeRestrictions_BODY exception): Block when label awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:SizeRestrictions_Body is present AND NOT (UriPath starts-with /checkout AND method=POST). Rule B (NoUserAgent_HEADER exception): Block when label awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:NoUserAgent_Header is present AND NOT ((UriPath=/home OR /catalog) AND method=GET). Enable SampledRequests and CloudWatch metrics on both.
**Purpose:** Re-enforce each sub-rule everywhere except its one confirmed false-positive scope, via scoped label-match rules deployed in Count first.
**Risks:** Rule B's exemption treats the empty-User-Agent client as legitimate; if 198.51.100.70 is NOT sanctioned, do not deploy Rule B.
**Advisory:** Keep each exception as narrow as the observed path+method., Optionally add a body-size constraint (~12 KB) for POST /checkout inside Rule A's exception so the exempt path is not unbounded.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm RuleActionOverrides is exactly SizeRestrictions_BODY=Count and…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1 --query 'WebACL.Rules[?Name==`AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet`].Statement.ManagedRuleGroupStatement.RuleActionOverrides'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm RuleActionOverrides is exactly SizeRestrictions_BODY=Count and NoUserAgent_HEADER=Count, no other sub-rule changed, and the two label rules exist after priority 3 in Count.

#### 4.2 Validate scope in Count before enforcing (Count-first guardrail), then…
**Type:** text
Over at least one full normal traffic cycle, watch the two label rules' CountedRequests and CommonRuleSet BlockedRequests in CloudWatch (AWS/WAFV2) and WAF logs (Athena default.waf_logs). Confirm each label rule matches every labelled request OUTSIDE its exempt scope and NONE inside it, and that 403s on POST /checkout and GET /home,/catalog from the affected clients have ceased. Only then should a human switch each label rule from Count to Block.
**Purpose:** Validate scope in Count before enforcing (Count-first guardrail), then switch to Block.
**Risks:** Switching to Block before validation could re-introduce the false positives or leave the sub-rules unenforced elsewhere.
**Advisory:** Switch Rule A and Rule B to Block in separate closely-watched changes; keep the reduced-protection window short.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Revert to the exact pre-change configuration, restoring both sub-rules…
**Type:** text
If the tuning misbehaves, re-read the LockToken and re-submit the exact original ruleset from waf-baseline.json: CommonRuleSet with no RuleActionOverrides (both sub-rules back to default Block) and no custom label rules. aws wafv2 update-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1 --lock-token <fresh-token> --default-action Allow --visibility-config <from baseline> --rules file://waf-baseline-rules.json
**Purpose:** Revert to the exact pre-change configuration, restoring both sub-rules to default Block and removing the custom label rules.
**Risks:** Rollback restores the original false-positive behavior: legitimate large POST /checkout and the empty-UA GETs will be blocked again until a corrected tuning is applied.
**Advisory:** Re-read the LockToken immediately before the rollback update; a stale token fails.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Keep legitimate /checkout request bodies within the WAF body-size limit (application-layer complement).
**Description:** SizeRestrictions_BODY blocks because legitimate POST /checkout bodies reach ~10,185 bytes, above CommonRuleSet's fixed 8,192-byte limit (not configurable). Reduce the checkout POST payload below 8 KB — trim redundant fields, compress/paginate large arrays, or move bulky data out of the form body.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Typical POST /checkout bodies are under 8,192 bytes in normal operation
- No legitimate checkout submission is blocked by SizeRestrictions_BODY even without the WAF exemption

#### 2. Make the sanctioned automated client send a proper User-Agent header (preferred fix for Cause 2).
**Description:** NoUserAgent_HEADER blocks client 198.51.100.70 because it sends an empty User-Agent on GET /home and /catalog. ONLY if the client is confirmed sanctioned/owned, configure it to send a descriptive non-empty User-Agent on every request — this restores NoUserAgent_HEADER coverage on those paths. If it cannot be changed, keep the scoped WAF exemption (Rule B).
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The automated client sends a non-empty, identifying User-Agent on all requests
- Its GET /home and /catalog requests are no longer labelled by NoUserAgent_HEADER
- Client ownership/identity of 198.51.100.70 is confirmed before any exemption or client change

   - Q-19 for any client with a BLOCK from an injection/bad-input/bot rule: report its ALLOW requests (residue / missed-by-rule).
   - A5 label-onset queries: when did the terminating labels first appear in the window vs baseline.
3. Budget ~15 queries. Report queries run and bytes scanned per query.

RETURN FORMAT (compact aggregates only — no raw records):
- Per query: ID, row count, bytes scanned, ~20 top rows (counts by rule/sub-rule/client/method/URI/label/time bucket).
- Payloads as CLASS and COUNT only (e.g. "sqli x75, xss x60, traversal-lfi x30") plus field location — never samples, matched-data strings, SQL keywords, or script tags. Apply the defang rule where the library says to.
- Q-20 split: per (sub-rule, verdict) the requests, distinct clients, field location, endpoint, first/last seen, and a pattern summary in words.
- Measured distinct client counts (Q-02 clients, Q-21 rows).
- Exact error code of anything that failed, and your Assumptions.

{"id": "f4a5118a-71a7-48e2-b1a9-36c099bc274b", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "743fc282-b588-44b3-a746-cd75011bccdd", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aws-waf-log-analysis
     3	description: >-
     4	  Use this skill when an investigation describes symptoms on a CloudFront distribution, Application
     5	  Load Balancer or API Gateway API and asks what the root cause is or what happened, even if AWS
     6	  WAF is never named: users, partners, webhooks, scripts or mobile apps get HTTP 403, 405 or 202
     7	  responses, empty responses or a 4xx spike; forms, uploads, reviews or listings are rejected; a
     8	  partner integration fails; requests look suspicious or malicious (SQL injection, XSS, scans,
     9	  bots); or an outage or timeouts hit the front door. It checks whether a Web ACL is in the path
     10	  (and continues the RCA when WAF is not the cause), finds which WAF rule, Anti-DDoS rule or Shield
     11	  Advanced mitigation blocked, challenged or only counted the requests and whether that is a false
     12	  positive, an attack or both, and hunts for threats WAF detected but did not block. Uses WAF logs
     13	  (CloudWatch Logs Insights or Athena), metrics and sampled requests; records evidence-backed
     14	  findings, advisory scoped fixes and a threat-hunt report.
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: lkna
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "AWS WAF, AWS Shield, Amazon CloudFront, Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon Athena"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Security, Networking"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# AWS WAF Log Analysis
     24	
     25	Find out whether AWS WAF (including Anti-DDoS rules and Shield Advanced automatic mitigation) caused a front-door symptom, and what it denied (Mode A); or hunt WAF logs for threats, including what WAF detected but did not block (Mode B).
     26	
     27	## Purpose and guarantees
     28	
     29	- **Read-only.** Use only Describe, Get and List calls, plus `logs:StartQuery`/`GetQueryResults`, `athena:StartQueryExecution` (SELECT only, when permitted)/`GetQueryResults`, `cloudtrail:LookupEvents`, `wafv2:GetSampledRequests` and `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`.
     30	- Never run DDL. Never change a Web ACL, rule, IP set, Shield setting, log configuration or any other resource.
     31	- **Advisory.** Describe fixes in prose for a human to review and apply. Never apply them.
     32	- **Single-turn.** Never ask the user a question and never wait for input. Apply "Defaults when input is missing", record every default under "Assumptions", and continue.
     33	- **Never stop on a gap.** A denied call or a missing table moves you to the next source or the degraded path.
     34	- **Exact errors.** Record the exact error code. Call something "not permitted" only on `AccessDenied`/`UnauthorizedOperation`.
     35	  - A cancelled, timed-out or throttled call is retried once, then reported as not completed.
     36	  - A tool refusal such as "service operations are not allowed" means: run the call in a subagent.
     37	- **Records are the deliverable** in both modes (symptoms, observations, findings, gaps, hypotheses); the last message closes them (see "Output").
     38	- **Final output.** Complete as delivered; never ends with a question or an offer. Never call `ask_user` (or any ask tool), not even after the answer to offer follow-up work or a fix: a turn that ends on a tool call loses the answer. Put follow-ups in "Next steps" and end on plain text.
     39	
     40	## Pick the mode from the request
     41	
     42	Inputs: the request text plus any incident or alarm details. A threat hunt needs no alarm. Record the mode under "Assumptions".
     43	
     44	Most requests never name WAF: they describe a symptom on a CloudFront distribution, ALB or API Gateway API and ask for the root cause or what happened. Do D-1 first. No Web ACL in the path: record `WAF_CLEARED` and continue the RCA to the actual cause (A0, "After `WAF_CLEARED`"). Otherwise classify:
     45	
     46	| Request contains | Mode |
     47	|---|---|
     48	| Denial or error symptoms: 403/405/202, empty responses, "blocked", "can't access", rejected forms, uploads or posts, a failing partner, webhook or integration, a 4xx/5xx spike, timeouts, an outage, or an alarm on a front-door resource | **Mode A**, starting with the A0 rule-out |
     49	| Suspicious traffic or hunting language: "malicious", "suspicious requests", "SQL injection", "scan", "attack", "bots", "what happened to these requests", "review WAF logs", "is WAF missing anything", a scheduled or recurring review | **Mode B** |
     50	| Both | Mode A first, then Mode B on the same window, focused on the slice Mode A found |
     51	| Neither, but the incident involves a resource that a Web ACL protects | **A0 rule-out only**; if A0 finds WAF implicated or inconclusive, continue with A1 to A7 |
     52	
     53	Mode A `CORRECT_MITIGATION`: recommend Mode B on that slice, or run it when hunting is in scope.
     54	
     55	## Defaults when input is missing
     56	
     57	Never ask; apply and record the default. Full table: "Defaults when input is missing (full table)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     58	
     59	- **Time window:** Mode A: incident start minus 30 min through now, capped at 24 h; no incident time: last 3 h. Mode B: last 7 days.
     60	- **Web ACL:** every ACL on the resources in the request; none identifiable: all ACLs (both scopes), top 3 by denying volume.
     61	- **Several tables or log groups:** the exact location match with the newest data.
     62	- **S3 logging but no table, or no logging:** don't stop; take the degraded path and report the gap with the advisory fix.
     63	- **Missing permission:** fall back to the next source and name the permission.
     64	
     65	## Discover
     66	
     67	Read [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) for D-1 to D-7 at the start of every run. Never ask for a resource or ACL.
     68	
     69	- **D-1 Resource to Web ACL:** CloudFront `GetDistributionConfig` `WebACLId`; regional resources `wafv2:GetWebACLForResource`.
     70	- **D-2 Read the ACL:** `wafv2:GetWebACL` for rule order, actions, managed groups and versions, `RuleActionOverrides`, Count overrides, scope-downs, custom responses, token domains, immunity times, IP set references, and any `ShieldMitigationRuleGroup_*` rule.
     71	- **D-2b Token posture:** classify P0 (no token-aware rules), P1 (token labels, no or only threshold-based enforcement) or P2 (strict token enforcement); confirm with Q-18.
     72	- **D-3 Log destination:** `wafv2:GetLoggingConfiguration`, including logging filters and redacted fields. Log group: Logs Insights. S3 or Firehose to S3: Athena. None, or a non-S3 destination without a full S3 backup: degraded path.
     73	- **D-4 Find the table or log group:** list tables in **every** Glue database, including `default`, across the Regions in D-4. Write "no table" only after that full listing. Never analyze raw log objects (`s3:GetObject`) as a substitute.
     74	- **D-7 Shield Advanced status:** `shield:DescribeSubscription`, `DescribeProtection` (L7AM status and action), `ListAttacks`/`DescribeAttack`, and `DDoSDetected` in `AWS/DDoSProtection`.
     75	
     76	**Region rule.** For CloudFront scope, the ACL, its logging configuration, its log group and its `AWS/WAFV2` metrics are in us-east-1. Only the Glue table and Athena follow the customer's setup; run Athena in the table's Region.
     77	
     78	## Bind schema and guard cost
     79	
     80	Queries are cited as `Q-NN (QA-NN / QI-NN)`; run the one for the backend from D-3 and D-4. Detail: "Schema binding and cost guards (detail)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     81	
     82	- **Athena:** bind `<table>`, `<req>`, label type and `<pf>` from `glue:GetTable`. The log subagent reads [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) "Schema binding" and the query sections it runs.
     83	- **Logs Insights:** the log subagent reads [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) "Conventions" and the query sections it runs.
     84	- **Probe first, in the log subagent.** The main agent runs no Athena query. On a probe error, take the degraded path.
     85	- **Cost:** prune partitions, start narrow, no unbounded `SELECT *`, at most one `UNNEST` per query.
     86	- **Budget:** about 15 log queries (about 10 on the Mode B fast path). Report queries run and bytes scanned.
     87	
     88	## Run it in AWS DevOps Agent
     89	
     90	The main agent discovers; subagents query. Read "Subagent briefs" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) before you start a log subagent, and when your prompt says discovery is done.
     91	
     92	**If your prompt says discovery is done and you are a subagent:** skip Steps 1 to 3, start no further subagents and do not load this skill again. Follow "Subagent briefs" for your role.
     93	
     94	**If you are a subagent without a discovery brief** (the platform handed you the whole task, so no main agent ran Steps 1 to 3): do the main agent's and the log subagent's work yourself, and start no further log subagent.
     95	
     96	1. Do D-1 to D-4. For D-4, call `glue:GetTables` on every database that `glue:GetDatabases` returns, including `default`, and match `Location` to the log prefix. A database list alone never means "no table".
     97	2. Never analyze raw S3 log objects, or sampled requests for a window that ended over 3 hours ago.
     98	3. Run the probe, then the mode's queries. Copy each query verbatim from [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) or [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) by searching for its ID (for example `QA-13b`). Never summarize the query references with a distill tool: summaries drop mandatory queries.
     99	4. In Mode B, run Q-13b and Q-19 whatever else you run. In both modes, run Q-20 for a sub-rule that matches payloads (blocking or in Count).
     100	5. Return the full Output block, so the agent that started you can pass it on verbatim.
     101	
     102	- [ ] Step 1: **Main agent: discover, bind, delegate.**
     103	  - Load this skill once and no other log-search or log-analysis skill. Read reference sections by search or offset.
     104	  - Do D-1 to D-4, D-2b and `glue:GetTable` (or find the log group) yourself.
     105	  - Start **one** log-analysis subagent (`preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis']` where supported) and the change subagent (Step 3) in the same turn.
     106	  - The brief carries everything bound, the mode and steps, the budget and the return format; neutral wording; a unique `name` per launch.
     107	- [ ] Step 2: **Main agent: no query libraries, no log queries.** Do metrics (A1, D-5) and Shield (D-7) while the subagent runs. At most one follow-up log pass, for a new uncharacterized candidate.
     108	- [ ] Step 3: **CloudTrail only in a change subagent, never in the main agent.**
     109	  - Every `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` (A5; "After `WAF_CLEARED`"; Mode B change correlation) runs in one change subagent.
     110	  - Launch: `agent_type` `generic`, `name` `change-timeline`, `preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis', 'investigating-infrastructure-changes']` (whichever are available).
     111	  - Always start it, even when memory or an earlier refusal says CloudTrail is blocked; mandatory for a rule-out request.
     112	  - Its prompt points it to "Change lookups" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) (Regions, event names, sweep, return contract).
     113	  - Write "blocked" or "denied" only on the change subagent's own `AccessDenied`.
     114	  - No completed lookup: write "changes: not checked (<reason>)". Never "no change", "ruled out" or "CloudTrail is blocked in this environment".
     115	- [ ] Step 4: **Subagents return compact aggregates only.** Per query: ID, row count, bytes scanned, about 20 top rows; payloads as class and count; never raw result sets or log records.
     116	- [ ] Step 5: **Refusal, failure or no subagent capability.**
     117	  - Relaunch a refused log or change subagent once, under a new name, with the same `preloaded_skills`.
     118	  - Change relaunch fails too: "changes: not checked (change subagent refused twice)".
     119	  - Log relaunch fails too, or no subagents: run about 10 count-only aggregate queries yourself and record the fallback.
     120	  - A3/A4 detail is then out of reach: say so and cap confidence at "low".
     121	
     122	## Rule and label knowledge
     123	
     124	Read L-1 in [label-reference.md](references/label-reference.md) when you need a rule or label meaning (in AWS DevOps Agent, inside the log subagent).
     125	
     126	- Order: `wafv2:DescribeManagedRuleGroup` with the ACL's version when permitted (opt-in; record a denial). Then exact label strings from Q-09 (casing can differ from rule names). Then the bundled, dated tables.
     127	- A connected AWS documentation tool may confirm semantics; never required.
     128	- A label found in neither the API output nor the bundled tables is "meaning unverified". Never infer meaning from its name.
     129	
     130	## Mode A: access-denied triage
     131	
     132	Read [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) when Mode A runs (step detail), and [remediation-patterns.md](references/remediation-patterns.md) (R-01 to R-11) at Step A7.
     133	
     134	- [ ] Step A0: **WAF rule-out**, cheapest first: Web ACL in the path; symptom type fits WAF; denying metrics and Shield or Anti-DDoS signals rose; Q-15 shows denials on the scope.
     135	  - Wording alone never clears WAF (a 202 with an empty body is often reported as "timeout").
     136	  - Only "no Web ACL in the path" stops the WAF checks at once; the change subagent still runs the origin-side checks.
     137	  - `WAF_CLEARED` never ends the RCA. Origin-side next steps are checks, not conclusions; name no root cause outside WAF that evidence does not show. An origin-side change whose time matches onset and recovery is the Root Cause, with the event evidence and load-balancer metrics; never stop at "out of scope".
     138	- [ ] Step A1: **Confirm involvement:** front-door 4xx versus `AWS/WAFV2` Blocked/Challenge/Captcha per rule, against the preceding window and the prior day, with request-volume stability. Never clear WAF on 4xx alone.
     139	- [ ] Step A2: **Attribute:** group terminating records by action, rule, managed sub-rule, response code and time bucket (Q-02, Q-01, Q-14 for Shield L7AM).
     140	- [ ] Step A3: **Client capability (Challenge/CAPTCHA only):** token posture and the path's token-status profile (Q-18, Q-05, Q-09, Q-04). Quote the `failureReason` value with its count (for example `TOKEN_MISSING`).
     141	- [ ] Step A4: **Profile who is affected:** clients, URIs and match details against allowed history before onset (Q-03, Q-04, Q-06, Q-07, Q-10, Q-12, Q-13). For blocked attackers, run Q-19; never "benign" without it.
     142	  - One profile per affected client or population (Q-21): IP, user agent, country (ASN if logged), paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen. Report the measured distinct client count; never assume distributed or single-source traffic.
     143	  - IP-set rule denies: read the set (`wafv2:GetIPSet`), name the matching entry, and say whether a similarly named allow set exists and which rule references it.
     144	- [ ] Step A5: **Correlate changes and events:** CloudTrail (change subagent), managed group versions, Anti-DDoS `event-detected` onset, Shield attacks (D-7). A version change or association is a cause only under the A5 evidence rules. No completed lookup: "changes: not checked".
     145	- [ ] Step A6: **Verdict** per denying (rule, action) pair: `FALSE_POSITIVE`, `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`, `CORRECT_MITIGATION` or `MIXED`; or overall `WAF_CLEARED` or `INCONCLUSIVE`. Give confidence (high, likely, low) and quantified impact. When legitimate users are reported denied and the logs cannot split a sub-rule's matches, the pair is `MIXED` (likely), never `CORRECT_MITIGATION`; judge request patterns, not whole clients.
     146	  - Missing allowed history is not evidence of attack. A monitor, health checker or integration with a benign profile hit by a header-presence or size rule is `FALSE_POSITIVE` (likely), with owner confirmation under "Verify before acting".
     147	  - **Payload split:** when a sub-rule (blocking or in Count) matches payloads, group its matches by pattern and field (Q-20), classify each pattern as attack or legitimate content (business text that only looks like SQL, script or JNDI), and report the split with counts ("Payload split inside one sub-rule" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md)).
     148	- [ ] Step A7: **Advise:** the narrowest R-xx fix, marked *reduces* or *eliminates*, validated in Count first (straight to Block only as R-01's labelled alternative).
     149	  - `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`: first a path scope-down of the challenge rule (R-05, covering every observed non-HTML path, including `/`), or token/SDK integration (R-06). Both rank above R-04.
     150	  - An IP or path is only a scope-down or exclusion on the challenge rule itself. Never add the client to an IP set used by an Allow-action rule.
     151	  - Never offer removing or disabling the Web ACL.
     152	
     153	## Mode B: threat hunting
     154	
     155	Read [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md) when Mode B runs; classify with [threat-taxonomy.md](references/threat-taxonomy.md) at Step B6. Detected-not-blocked is a priority finding (threat labels on ALLOW, Count-mode matches, rate rules in Count, attacker residue). A logging filter that drops ALLOW records limits the analysis: say so.
     156	
     157	- [ ] Step B1: **Fast path first** for a window of 2 hours or less, or one specific question: about 10 fixed queries, started together, polled once. The full set is in "Fast path".
     158	  - Q-13b is mandatory. It sets the top talker apart so a short burst cannot hide.
     159	  - Every sensitive-path burst and every client over a rate-rule limit is a finding with method, URI, count, peaks and first to last seen. Never "ordinary", "normal" or "a retry burst".
     160	  - Run the full funnel only for candidates the fast path cannot settle.
     161	- [ ] Step B2: **B0 Known automation:** high-volume, low-diversity clients with corroboration, excluded from baselines (Q-13, Q-12, Q-01). Report them under a required "Known automation" heading. Never label them card testing or abuse. Never exclude a population with token-reuse or coordinated-activity labels.
     162	- [ ] Step B3: **B-A Overview and B-B Standouts:** time series, breakdowns and label frequency (Q-01, Q-02, Q-03, Q-09); then standouts ranked numerically (Q-08, Q-11, Q-12, Q-14, Q-16b, Q-17).
     163	- [ ] Step B4: **Attacker residue (B-B):** for every client with any BLOCK from an injection, bad-input or bot rule, report its ALLOW requests as a missed-by-rule finding (Q-19).
     164	  - Never "benign", "clean" or "accounted for" unless Q-19 showed `args_class` `none` on application paths.
     165	  - Explain a miss only from the rule's documented inspection target (L-1); otherwise "reason not determined".
     166	  - Copy the field location verbatim. A query-argument residue needs a query-string rule; a `UriPath` rule does not cover it.
     167	  - **Count-mode payload split:** for every injection or bad-input sub-rule in Count, run Q-20 and split its matches by pattern and field: the attack part is "detected, not blocked"; the legitimate-content part is a false positive that must stay unblocked.
     168	- [ ] Step B5: **B-C to B-E Drill, narrow, confirm:** re-pivot one standout; one line per Count or rate-rule client (Q-08c); narrow to one client, rule or endpoint; confirm with Q-10 or Q-16b/Q-16.
     169	  - A burst on a payment, checkout, login, signup or password-reset URI is a card-testing or credential-stuffing finding whatever its size. Fix it with a path-scoped R-10 on that URI, Count first.
     170	- [ ] Step B6: **B-F and B-G:** resolve load-bearing labels (L-1; unverified stays unverified), map each signature to a class and an R-xx mitigation, and hand legitimate-user denials to Mode A.
     171	- [ ] Step B7: **Record, then generate the hunting report.** Write the Mode B records first ("Records" under "Output"). If the runtime can create a report artifact, write the report as a Markdown artifact, following the section order and tables of [assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md](assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md) exactly; load it first:
     172	  ```
     173	  read_skill_resource(skill_id="aws-waf-log-analysis", path="assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md")
     174	  ```
     175	  - The records stay the primary deliverable; the report repeats their numbers and adds no finding.
     176	  - No artifact capability: put the same sections into the final message, after the Output template block.
     177	  - **If the `read_skill_resource` call fails**, note at the top of the report "report template (`assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md`) could not be loaded; structure follows the Mode B contract", and still produce the sections of "Output (Mode B contract)" in [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md).
     178	
     179	## Degraded path
     180	
     181	Use when WAF logs can't be queried (no table, no logging, a non-S3 destination, a missing permission); the investigation continues. Read D-5 in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     182	
     183	- **WAF metrics** say *whether* WAF denied and *which rule*, not *who* or *which path*. **Sampled requests:** last 3 hours only, examples rather than counts.
     184	- **Confidence:** cap at "likely" (A0 structural clears can be high). With Shield L7AM attached, a metric-based clear is `INCONCLUSIVE`. Lower to "low" when A3 or A4 cannot be assessed.
     185	- **Wrap-up:** state that WAF logs weren't analyzed and why, with the advisory fix (D-6 DDL, logging configuration, or the missing permission).
     186	
     187	## Output
     188	
     189	Read [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md) before you write any record, handoff or final answer (record rules, last-message rules, mitigation handoff). Mode sections are in the mode references.
     190	
     191	**Template.** The main agent's very last message closes the investigation, in every mode and verdict, including any reply after the mitigation step. It starts with `Assumptions:` (no preface) and repeats this block even if earlier messages carried it:
     192	
     193	```
     194	Assumptions: window; Web ACLs; backend; mode; defaults, fallbacks, calls not completed (exact error)
     195	Verdict: <Mode A: per (rule, action), or WAF_CLEARED / INCONCLUSIVE; Mode B: per confirmed finding> (confidence: high | likely | low)
     196	Evidence: <key numbers from the log subagent's table (step-5 fallback: your recorded results), with query IDs>; Changes (CloudTrail): <per category, Regions/sources/names searched: events found | none found>; origin-side: not checked (<reason>) if not searched | not checked (<reason>) | not applicable (Mode B)
     197	AI-generated: findings need human verification before anyone acts on them.
     198	```
     199	
     200	Then the mode sections, the findings, the next steps, and a last line `Ruled out: <each hypothesis, with the evidence that closed it, or "still open">`.
     201	
     202	**Counts.** Copy every count from the log subagent's table; never recompute or round. Memory is never evidence.
     203	
     204	**Records.** Platform records are the judged deliverable in both modes. In both:
     205	
     206	- one observation record per key result first (counts, window, baseline, query ID), so findings can cite them;
     207	- exactly one Root Cause;
     208	- every Cause and Root Cause finding lists those observation IDs in its supporting observations (never empty) and the Web ACL in its related resources;
     209	- a gap record per denied or not-completed call or unassessed step; closed hypotheses with their evidence.
     210	
     211	Mode A: one symptom per burst and per affected client or population (IP, user agent, paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen; never merge clients or rules); one Cause per denying (rule, action) pair, titled with the exact rule and sub-rule ID and the verdict, naming the matching resource (IP set and entry).
     212	
     213	Both modes: a payload split gives one Cause per (sub-rule, verdict), or one `MIXED` Cause listing both parts with counts, field and pattern summary.
     214	
     215	Mode B (full rules in "Mode B records" in [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md)):
     216	
     217	- one Symptom per distinct activity pattern: window, client, method and path, counts;
     218	- one Cause per confirmed threat finding, titled with class, client and exact rule and sub-rule IDs, or "not matched by any rule", or "detected, not blocked: <rate rule> in Count";
     219	- known automation as an observation plus a closed hypothesis, never a threat finding;
     220	- the Root Cause is the overall assessment: what WAF caught, what it missed and why (for example a rate rule in Count), naming every Cause, linking their observations and any known-automation observation, with WAF-layer and Application-layer mitigations (path-scoped R-10 first for card testing; when known automation exceeds the site-wide rate rule, one sentence that it stays in Count and why).
     221	
     222	**Mitigation guardrails** (every message, finding and handoff):
     223	
     224	- Never disable or remove a rule group or the Web ACL.

     2	
     3	Read-only SELECT queries for investigating WAF activity. Bind the placeholders once from the table definition, then reuse them in every query. All times are UTC; the WAF `timestamp` field is milliseconds since epoch.
     4	
     5	## Schema binding (do this first)
     6	
     7	In AWS DevOps Agent the main agent binds these from `glue:GetTable` and passes them in (SKILL.md, "Bind schema and guard cost"); bind them yourself only if they are missing.
     8	
     9	1. **`<req>`:** `httprequest.` for a nested request struct (for example `httprequest.clientip`), empty for flat top-level fields. The SQL below puts `<req>` in front of `clientip`, `uri`, `args`, `httpmethod`, `country` and `headers`.
     10	2. **Label type:** `array<struct<name>>` means `x.name`, as written below. For `array<string>`, change the lambdas `x -> x.name` to `x -> x`, and the UNNEST aliases `l.name` and `co.name` to `l` and `co`.
     11	3. **`<pf>`** from `projection.<key>.format` and `storage.location.template`: projection key `log_time`, format `yyyy/MM/dd/HH/mm` gives `log_time BETWEEN '2026/10/06/17/30' AND '2026/10/06/18/30'`; a non-projected `date` key gives `date BETWEEN '2026/10/06' AND '2026/10/07'`. `SHOW CREATE TABLE` is not needed.
     12	4. **Rules.**
     13	   - Use at most one `UNNEST` per query.
     14	   - Always include `<pf>`; keep the window tight.
     15	   - Add `AND webaclid = '<arn>'` when several web ACLs share a bucket.
     16	   - Report `DataScannedInBytes` for every query you run.
     17	   - Only run SELECT/WITH statements.
     18	5. **Pick the workgroup, run, and poll.**
     19	   - Workgroup: the one named in the request; otherwise one with managed query results enabled (`athena:ListWorkGroups`, then `athena:GetWorkGroup` and check `Configuration.ManagedQueryResultsConfiguration.Enabled`); otherwise `primary`. Record the choice under "Assumptions".
     20	   - Run `athena:StartQueryExecution` in the table's Region with that workgroup.
     21	   - Poll `athena:GetQueryExecution` once per query ID (not `athena:BatchGetQueryExecution`, which the README add-on policy does not grant) until `Status.State` is `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELLED`. Read `Statistics.DataScannedInBytes` from that response (the cost guard), then read rows with `athena:GetQueryResults` only after `SUCCEEDED`.
     22	   - On an output-location, workgroup or permission error: record the error, include the bound SQL as advisory text, and continue on the degraded path (D-5 in `discovery-and-log-sources.md`).
     23	
     24	`<table>` is the `database.table` name resolved from `glue:GetTable`. When no incident time is known, build the `<pf>` window from the skill's default-window rules (SKILL.md, "Defaults when input is missing").
     25	
     26	Placeholders: `<table>`, `<pf>`, `<req>`, `<ip>`, `<uri>`, `<host>`, `<rule>` (terminating rule or rule group), `<sub_rule>` (rule inside a managed group), `<focus_label>`, `<token_id_prefix>` (first 12 characters of a token id from QA-16b).
     27	
     28	Note on `<sub_rule>`: for a request stopped inside a rule group, `terminatingruleid` is the group and the inner rule is in `rulegrouplist`. The expression `element_at(filter(rulegrouplist, g -> g.terminatingrule IS NOT NULL), 1).terminatingrule.ruleid` extracts it.
     29	
     30	---
     31	
     32	### QA-01 — What happened when? (action by 5-minute bucket)
     33	
     34	**Use when:** you need the shape of an incident: when blocking started and stopped, and whether allowed traffic dipped.
     35	
     36	```sql
     37	SELECT from_unixtime(floor(timestamp / 1000 / 300) * 300) AS bucket, action, count(*) AS requests
     38	FROM <table> WHERE <pf>
     39	GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
     40	```
     41	
     42	**Interpret:** Normal is a steady ALLOW series with few or no denials. A block, CAPTCHA or CHALLENGE series that starts and ends sharply marks an event window; use its first and last bucket as the window for later queries. A drop in ALLOW at the same time as a rise in BLOCK warrants QA-02 and QA-04 to tell whether legitimate clients are affected; the buckets alone do not say.
     43	
     44	### QA-02 — What is denying traffic? (terminating rules and sub-rules)
     45	
     46	**Use when:** you need to know which rule (and which rule inside a managed group) is blocking or challenging requests, and how many clients are affected.
     47	
     48	```sql
     49	SELECT action, terminatingruleid AS rule,
     50	       coalesce(element_at(filter(rulegrouplist, g -> g.terminatingrule IS NOT NULL), 1).terminatingrule.ruleid, '-') AS sub_rule,
     51	       responsecodesent AS response_code,
     52	       count(*) AS requests, count(DISTINCT <req>clientip) AS clients,
     53	       min(from_unixtime(timestamp / 1000)) AS first_seen, max(from_unixtime(timestamp / 1000)) AS last_seen
     54	FROM <table>
     55	WHERE <pf> AND action IN ('BLOCK', 'CAPTCHA', 'CHALLENGE')
     56	GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
     57	ORDER BY requests DESC
     58	LIMIT 50
     59	```
     60	
     61	**Interpret:** One rule with very few clients and a bounded first/last window points to a single source. Many clients on one sub-rule points to a broad pattern or a false positive on legitimate users. `response_code` may be populated (for example a custom response code, or 202 for Challenge as seen in testing) or empty; when empty, assume the defaults: BLOCK = 403, CAPTCHA = 405, CHALLENGE = 202. Request counts can lag slightly because of late log delivery. Rule IDs and label strings differ in casing and namespace (for example rule `SizeRestrictions_BODY` produces label `awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:SizeRestrictions_Body`). Never construct a label from a rule ID; copy the exact string from QA-09 or from DescribeManagedRuleGroup.
     62	
     63	### QA-03 — Who is affected by one sub-rule? (affected population)
     64	
     65	**Use when:** you have a `<sub_rule>` from QA-02 and need to see who triggers it: IPs, countries, user agents, methods, URIs, TLS fingerprint.
     66	
     67	```sql
     68	SELECT <req>clientip AS client_ip, <req>country AS country,
     69	       element_at(filter(<req>headers, h -> lower(h.name) = 'user-agent'), 1).value AS ua,
     70	       <req>httpmethod AS method, <req>uri AS uri, ja4fingerprint AS ja4, count(*) AS requests
     71	FROM <table>
     72	WHERE <pf>
     73	  AND element_at(filter(rulegrouplist, g -> g.terminatingrule IS NOT NULL), 1).terminatingrule.ruleid = '<sub_rule>'
     74	GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 ORDER BY requests DESC LIMIT 50
     75	```
     76	
     77	**Interpret:** One IP with a browser-like user agent on one method and URI is a single client repeating a request. Many IPs sharing one user agent and JA4 value suggests a tool or botnet. A missing user agent (empty `ua`) is itself a signal for header-based rules. Use the same pattern with `terminatingruleid = '<rule>'` for rules that are not inside a group.
     78	
     79	### QA-04 — What did the denied clients do when allowed? (allowed history)
     80	
     81	**Use when:** you need to know whether the denied clients also sent allowed requests, which separates abuse from a rule that is simply too strict.
     82	
     83	```sql
     84	WITH denied AS (
     85	  SELECT DISTINCT <req>clientip AS ip FROM <table>
     86	  WHERE <pf>
     87	    AND element_at(filter(rulegrouplist, g -> g.terminatingrule IS NOT NULL), 1).terminatingrule.ruleid = '<sub_rule>')
     88	SELECT w.action, w.<req>httpmethod AS method, w.<req>uri AS uri,
     89	       count(*) AS requests, count(DISTINCT w.<req>clientip) AS clients
     90	FROM <table> w JOIN denied d ON w.<req>clientip = d.ip
     91	WHERE <pf>
     92	GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY requests DESC LIMIT 50
     93	```
     94	
     95	**Interpret:** A client that sent normal ALLOW requests (for example GET pages) and is blocked only on one method and URI suggests that specific request shape trips the rule. A client that is only ever denied suggests dedicated abuse traffic.
     96	
     97	### QA-05 — Challenge and CAPTCHA behavior
     98	
     99	**Not validated with data in testing:** the test table had no challenge or CAPTCHA rows, so the query was only confirmed to execute.
     100	
     101	**Use when:** challenges or CAPTCHAs are in play and you need to see failure reasons, which clients receive them and whether they carry a WAF token.
     102	
     103	```sql
     104	SELECT action, challengeresponse.failurereason AS challenge_failure, captcharesponse.failurereason AS captcha_failure,
     105	       <req>httpmethod AS method,
     106	       coalesce(element_at(filter(<req>headers, h -> lower(h.name) = 'accept'), 1).value, '(none)') AS accept,
     107	       coalesce(element_at(filter(<req>headers, h -> lower(h.name) = 'user-agent'), 1).value, '(none)') AS ua,
     108	       cardinality(filter(<req>headers, h -> lower(h.name) = 'x-aws-waf-token')) > 0
     109	         OR any_match(<req>headers, h -> lower(h.name) = 'cookie' AND h.value LIKE '%aws-waf-token=%') AS has_token,
     110	       count(*) AS requests, count(DISTINCT <req>clientip) AS clients
     111	FROM <table>
     112	WHERE <pf> AND action IN ('CHALLENGE', 'CAPTCHA')
     113	GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 ORDER BY requests DESC LIMIT 50
     114	```
     115	
     116	**Interpret:** No rows means no challenge or CAPTCHA action in the window. Challenged `POST` or non-HTML (`accept` is JSON or empty) requests commonly fail because API clients cannot run the challenge script. Many `has_token = false` rows with a failure reason point to clients that never completed the challenge. Check `has_token`, `accept` and `ua` together before concluding that real users are affected.
     117	
     118	### QA-06 — What exactly matched? (match details)
     119	
     120	**Use when:** you need the matched condition and sample data behind a blocking rule.

{"id": "4b862a04-05e7-4253-b454-07b47839a9dd", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_WGKnfn2ScIhB88ob9H1Kd6", "content": [{"text": "     120	**Use when:** you need the matched condition and sample data behind a blocking rule.
     121	
     122	```sql
     123	SELECT d.conditiontype, d.location,
     124	       transform(slice(d.matcheddata, 1, 5), m -> substr(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(m, '(?i)%(3c|3e|22|27|60|3b)', '_'), '[<>"''`;(){}$|]', '_'), 1, 40)) AS sample_defanged,
     125	       count(*) AS requests
     126	FROM <table>
     127	CROSS JOIN UNNEST(coalesce(element_at(filter(rulegrouplist, g -> g.terminatingrule IS NOT NULL), 1).terminatingrule.rulematchdetails,
     128	                           terminatingrulematchdetails)) AS x(d)
     129	WHERE <pf> AND action = 'BLOCK'
     130	GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY requests DESC LIMIT 50
     131	```
     132	
     133	**Interpret:** Match details are not logged for every rule type. In testing, size-restriction and header-presence rules returned no rows here; that is normal, not an error. **Validated in testing:** SQLi rules logged `SQL_INJECTION` with `sensitivitylevel` `LOW` and a `location` (`ALL_QUERY_ARGS` or `BODY`); XSS rules logged `XSS` with no sensitivity level; regex-based rules (path traversal, SSRF, Log4J header) logged `REGEX` with locations such as `ALL_QUERY_ARGS`, `QUERY_STRING` or `ANY_HEADER`. For rules that log no details, use QA-03 and QA-07 to characterize the requests instead. When rows appear, `location` and `sample_defanged` show which part of the request matched; the sample is defanged in the query (special characters replaced, at most 40 characters per element; the `transform` is not validated), and never re-read raw `matcheddata`. `sample_defanged` is for use inside the querying subagent only (to classify the match); return class, count and `location` to the main agent, never the sample.
     134	
     135	### QA-07 — Body size and oversize profile
     136	
     137	**Use when:** a body-size or oversize-related rule is blocking, or you suspect requests exceed the inspection limit.
     138	
     139	```sql
     140	SELECT <req>uri AS uri, oversizefields, approx_percentile(requestbodysize, 0.5) AS p50_body,
     141	       max(requestbodysize) AS max_body, max(requestbodysizeinspectedbywaf) AS max_inspected, count(*) AS requests
     142	FROM <table>
     143	WHERE <pf> AND requestbodysize > 0
     144	GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY requests DESC LIMIT 50
     145	```
     146	
     147	**Interpret:** Most URIs show small bodies. A URI whose `max_body` is far above its `p50_body` is where large requests concentrate. Compare `max_inspected` with `max_body`: if inspection stops at the web ACL's body limit while the body is larger, the remainder is not inspected. A non-empty `oversizefields` means WAF could not inspect all of that component. Empty `oversizefields` with a large body means the body was inspected in full.
     148	
     149	### QA-08 — Count-mode and non-terminating matches
     150	
     151	**Use when:** you want to know which rules are matching without blocking (Count mode), including rate-based rules that never reached their limit action.
     152	
     153	```sql
     154	SELECT r.ruleid, r.action, count(*) AS requests
     155	FROM <table> CROSS JOIN UNNEST(nonterminatingmatchingrules) AS x(r)
     156	WHERE <pf>
     157	GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY requests DESC LIMIT 50
     158	```
     159	
     160	**Interpret:** A Count rule with very high volume may reflect heavy traffic from a few sources (for example a load test or shared NAT address), but volume alone does not make it benign. Corroborate with QA-13 (small fixed URI set, stable JA4, steady rate over a long period, no other threat labels) before treating the source as known automation, and still report it. A Count rule that matches mostly the same clients as a later block is a candidate for blocking. No rows means no top-level Count-mode activity; run QA-08b for rule groups.
     161	
     162	#### QA-08b — Rule-group Count matches (Athena only)
     163	
     164	A separate query, because only one UNNEST is allowed. Logs Insights has no separate rule-group query: QI-08 covers both the top-level and the rule-group lists.
     165	
     166	```sql
     167	SELECT g.rulegroupid, cardinality(g.nonterminatingmatchingrules) AS n_rules, count(*) AS requests
